subject: Co-term request & early-exit refund scenarios for multi-year prepay
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@datascale.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@datascale.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Question on early-exit refunds & co-terming for multi-year prepay

Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement's dug into the multi-year prepay proposal (3-year, annual drawdown ramps) and we have two items blocking approval:

1) If we need to exit after year 1 or 2, what's Redwood's refund or credit policy? Do you pro-rate remaining prepay or retain a termination fee? We need something that maps to our ASC 606 accounting expectations.

2) We have an existing Redwood pilot contract that renews on 12/31/2027. We'd prefer to co-term the new committed capacity to that date rather than run parallel renewal dates — is that supported and how would the economics align (prorated credits, true-up)?

Can you send scenarios (year-by-year example) showing refunds, credit usage, and any termination charges? Procurement would like this for their steering committee on Tuesday.

Thanks — Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Procurement | DataScale Inc
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@datascale.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@datascale.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Question on early-exit refunds & co-terming for multi-year prepay

Liam —

Appreciate the clear asks. I put together three practical options (attached spreadsheet) and a preferred approach from our finance/contracting side. High level:

- Option A (pro-rate + admin fee): Remaining prepaid balance is returned as a credit less a 10% administrative termination charge; credits can be applied to hosted usage or future invoices within 12 months.
- Option B (non-refundable prepay with scaled refund): Refund equals remaining prepaid value less a declining termination fee schedule (Year1: 40%; Year2: 25%; Year3: 0%). Useful when customers want stronger price protection up front.
- Option C (co-term + true-up): Allow co-terming with prorated credit applied to align renewal date. No cash refund; instead we issue pro-rata credits toward the co-term period and offer a one-time onboarding credit to offset friction.

Attached: Redwood_Econ_Options_v3.xlsx (scenario tables), DS_Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf (MAP draft)

We recommend Option C for accounts that want clean renewal alignment (less cash churn, simpler accounting). I'll loop in finance to confirm ASC/IFRS-friendly language for the contract. Can we schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the numbers?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Econ_Options_v3.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@datascale.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@datascale.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Question on early-exit refunds & co-terming for multi-year prepay

Vanessa,

Thanks — Option C sounds promising. A few quick clarifying Qs before the call:

- For co-term true-up, is the pro-rata credit recognized immediately or amortized over the remaining co-term period? Our accounting team wants to avoid large revenue reversals.
- If we co-term on 12/31/2027 and our committed capacity ramps in Year 2, will Redwood allow usage credits to move between years (i.e., carry-forward) if we underuse in Year 1?

Also, can you share representative contract language for the 'early-exit credit' so our legal team can review redlines?

Priya Sharma
Sr. Finance Manager | DataScale Inc
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@datascale.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Question on early-exit refunds & co-terming for multi-year prepay

Priya —

Answers inline:

- Accounting treatment: Our finance team prefers credits (Option C) to avoid cash reversals; credits are recognized on invoice date and can be amortized per your accounting policy — we can reflect language that allows amortization over the remaining co-term.

- Carry-forward: We support carry-forward of unused prepaid units within the committed term up to 12 months; beyond that, credits expire unless otherwise negotiated.

- Contract language: See attached redlines (redlines_20260713.docx). Key clauses:
   * Early Exit Credit: 'Customer may request termination prior to the Co-Term Date. In such event, Redwood will calculate a pro-rata credit for unused prepaid commitment and apply a termination allowance equal to X% as set forth in Exhibit A.'
   * Co-Terming: 'Parties agree to align Renewal Date to Customer's target date. Any difference in term lengths shall be reconciled via pro-rata credits or true-up invoices.'

I've also proposed a compromise: a 20% termination allowance for Year1 exits, 10% for Year2, 0% thereafter, with credits expiring after 12 months. If that sounds reasonable I'll ask contracting to draft formal amendment language. Suggest a 30-min slot at 3:00pm PT today — dropping a calendar invite now.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redlines_20260713.docx (docx)
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@datascale.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 16:58:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Question on early-exit refunds & co-terming for multi-year prepay

Vanessa,

Thanks — the compromise sounds fair. Two final asks from procurement/legal before we proceed to amendment:

1) Please convert the Exhibit A termination schedule into a simple table in the SPA so the numbers are clear.
2) We need a DocuSign envelope for the amendment + MAP so our GC can sign remotely. Can you send by EOD tomorrow?

If you can get contracting to bake the amortization-friendly language in, we should be able to move to exec approvals this week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Liam
